title: fix(plugin-view): ObjectView fetches only for views that draw the rows, and a re-read keeps them on screen (objectui#10982)
body:
Fixes #10982

Clause-②: no

## What this changes

`ObjectView` fetches the rows for its non-grid views itself and hands them to the inner view as `data`. Both halves of the card land in `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`, which is the producer; no other package moves.

### (b) The fetch runs only for view types whose renderer draws the rows

`fetchDrawsView` was a deny-list (`grid`, `tree`, `chart`) that gated only the data-invalidation subscription, and the fetch itself was gated on `grid` alone. There is now one allow-list, `VIEW_TYPES_DRAWING_FETCHED_ROWS` = `kanban`, `calendar`, `gallery`, `timeline`, `map`, declared beside the host-composition view-type record. It gates both the subscription and the fetch.

The list comes from reading each `generateViewSchema` case AND the registered renderer that case resolves to. I did not copy it from the card:

- `object-kanban`, `object-calendar` and `object-map` spread the `data` prop into their component, and `object-gallery` / `object-timeline` read `props.data`. Each one draws the array it is handed.
- `object-gantt`'s registered wrapper (`ObjectGanttRenderer`) passes `ObjectGantt` the schema and nothing else. The chart never sees the array and queries for itself. plugin-gantt already pins this (`ObjectGantt.hostDataProp-7210.test.tsx`), and `ListView`'s `surfaceDrawsFetchedRows` rests on the same measurement. **This is where the card's premise was incomplete.** The old deny-list and the comment beside it both treated `gantt` as data-fed, so every gantt `object-view` was read on mount and again on every bus event, and nothing drew those rows.
- `object-tree` runs its own full query before it looks at any rows it is handed (objectui#10778). `object-chart` never reads them.
- `page`, `list` and `detail` are `ViewType` members with no `generateViewSchema` case. They fall through to `ObjectGrid`, which queries for itself.

Every renderer outside the list reads the bus itself. Every site that moves `refreshKey` also notifies the bus (`announceOwnWrite` and the `onMutation` subscription), so none of them loses its refresh.

**Scope, stated plainly.** The card names the bus subscription. The same allow-list now also gates the mount / `refreshKey` fetch, because that read has the same defect: rows that nothing draws. The dispatch route also asked that "a new view type fetches only when its case is added to both". Measured on the base (the reverse-verification run below): `tree` and `chart` were read once on mount, and `gantt`, `page`, `list` and `detail` were read on mount and again on the bus event. The tree cost more than that. With a real `object-tree` under `ObjectView`, the base made **3** reads: one by `ObjectView`, plus two by the tree itself, because the rows arriving changed the tree's `data` dependency and re-ran its query. At this head it makes **1**, the tree's own. That was a one-time probe with both legs restored and verified by blob hash; it is not a permanent test.

### (c) A re-read keeps the rows on screen

The fetch used to set `loading` to true on every run. Each run now names its request: object, resolved filter, sort and expansion. The rest of the `find` params are constant. If a run's request equals the one that the rows in `data` answer, it is a **re-read**: it leaves `loading` false and replaces the rows when the new ones arrive. Any other run sets `loading` true as before. That covers a first load, and also a change of filter, sort, expansion or object.

- `loading` is set on every run, false included. So a re-read that supersedes a first load still in flight shows the rows it already has, not a placeholder the superseded run left behind.
- No fallback hides an error. A failed re-read is handled exactly like a failed first load: `console.error`, `loading` ends false, and the rows already drawn stay.
- The `find` params stay an inline object literal. The first draft extracted them into a variable, which would have taken this call out of `no-unprefixed-query-params` (that rule reads only an inline literal) and out of the `QueryParams` excess-property check. Commit `1d75b57b5` put them back and keys the request on the inputs instead.

Which renderers honour a `loading` prop from this component: `object-calendar` (only alongside an array `data`, as its registration declares) is the one that swaps rows for a placeholder. `ObjectKanban` stores it but no render path reads it, and the gallery, timeline and map ignore it.

## Pins

- **New:** `ObjectView.fetchAllowList-10982.test.tsx`, 16 tests, through the real `SchemaRenderer` and registry:
  - For each of the five drawing types (control): read on mount, re-read exactly once on a bus event.
  - For each of `gantt`, `tree`, `chart`, `page`, `list` and `detail`: never read by this component, on mount or on a bus event, while the bare bus reader beside it moves. The inner view or the grid stand-in is asserted rendered and the schema read settled, so the zero is not vacuous.
  - Calendar: a bus re-read never paints the placeholder; the first load does (control).
  - Calendar: a re-read after an `onMutation` write never paints the placeholder.
  - Control: a changed request (a new filter) still paints it.
  - Calendar: a failed re-read logs the rejected error, keeps the rows and paints no placeholder, and the next event re-reads normally.
  - Control: a failed first load is logged and does not leave the placeholder up.
- **Corrected:** `ObjectView.busReread-10887.test.tsx`. Its stand-in drew the handed rows for `gantt`, which the real wrapper never forwards, so `gantt` leaves the re-read list and becomes a "not re-read" control through the authored path.
- **Corrected:** `ObjectView.refreshInPlace-10035.test.tsx`. Its stand-in modelled `tree` as drawing the handed rows. `tree` moves to the self-fetching group and keeps the same three assertions: same instance, refetched rows, one refetch per write.

## Reverse verification (one-time; no permanent test)

With the pins committed at `3e312c6a8`, the base `ObjectView.tsx` (blob `08747a478`) was written over the file and confirmed by blob hash. The three pin files were then run, and the file was restored with `git checkout HEAD --` under a trap and verified (blob equals HEAD's, `git diff HEAD` empty). The prediction was written down before the run: 9 red in the new file, the gantt control red in `busReread-10887`, and `refreshInPlace-10035` all green (it is a model correction and does not discriminate). Observed: **10 failed / 31 passed**, exactly those.
- `the gantt view was read for rows its renderer never draws: … called 2 times`, and similarly `tree` 1, `chart` 1, `page` 2, `list` 2, `detail` 2.
- `the bus re-read swapped the rows on screen for the placeholder: expected [ { placeholder: true, rows: 1 } ] to deeply equal []`
- The same `{ placeholder: true, rows: 1 }` paint on the `onMutation` re-read and on the failed re-read.

`ObjectView.tsx` is imported by relative path in these suites, so no build sat between the mutation and the run.

Each paragraph has been read: none is falsified by this diff, because they describe `generateViewSchema`, the grid node's `title` and the key census, none of which moves.

## Acceptance notes

- **Observation, not filed.** Read from the component's initial state, not measured in the UI. `loading` starts false with `data` as `[]`, so a calendar handed rows paints an empty calendar for the window before the object schema settles, and only then the first-load placeholder. Base and head behave the same. Starting `loading` true is not a mechanical change: an `object-view` with no object or adapter would then sit on the placeholder forever. Out of scope here; carrier: none.
- **Same-file neighbours.** The objectui#10993 branch edits the `@object-ui/i18n` import line, adds a top-level `useObjectTranslation` hook, and changes `getFormTitle` in this file. None of those regions is touched here. objectui#10976 is queued behind this card on the same file. Whichever lands second merges `origin/main` (merge commit, no rebase) and re-runs its gates.
- `ObjectView`'s comments that described `gantt` as drawing handed rows and `tree` as re-querying on the handed array are corrected in place. They were the text the old deny-list was reasoned from.
